samples.summary: New merge-budget enforcement and batch merge overlay in YorkieStore have no test at all
samples.evidence: `setMerge` now returns a boolean, spends `mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(others), [span])` against a `projectedMerges()` map, and `beginBatch`/`endBatch` maintain a new `batchMerges` overlay that `deleteMerge` also reads. I grepped packages/frontend/tests for `setMerge`, `batchMerges`, `projectedMerges`, `deleteMerge`, `merge`, and `YorkieStore` — the only YorkieStore suites are yorkie-axis-order, yorkie-cut-paste and yorkie-store-read-only, none of which touch merges. So nothing exercises: the re-anchor exclusion (`key !== sref`), the overlay-vs-document projection during a multi-block paste, or the false return path. If any of it is wrong, a user's merge (or a whole paste's merge layout) is silently dropped or double-counted with no failing test. Frontend also has no tsc lane, so even a type-level slip here is unguarded.

samples.summary: XLSX importer's new merge-budget drop path is untested
samples.evidence: `applyMergeRanges` now accumulates a budget and `continue`s past any `mergeCell` that `mergeBudgetAdmits` rejects — silently discarding merges from an imported file. packages/sheets/test/import/xlsx-importer.test.ts only has the pre-existing single `<mergeCell ref="A1:B1"/>` case (line 59/103); no fixture has an oversized span, >MaxMergeEntries mergeCells, or an over-covered map. A regression here (e.g. off-by-one accumulation, or budget seeded wrong) would silently lose merges from ordinary imports without any test noticing.

samples.summary: canMergeSelection's entry-count / covered-cells budget rejection is untested; only the per-span cap is
samples.evidence: merge.test.ts 'refuses a selection the budget cannot afford' selects rs = MaxMergedCells + 1, which trips the per-span `cells > MaxMergedCells` branch inside `mergeBudgetAdmits` — it never exercises the new `this.mergeBudget` accumulation (entries/coveredCells maintained in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`). No test builds a sheet with many existing merges and checks that the next merge is refused, so if `mergeBudget` were never updated (or reset) the suite would stay green.
searchedFor: read packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts merge budget describe block

samples.summary: Engine-side budget skip inside applyPasteMerges is untested (only the store-refusal path is)
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges` has two independent drop paths: `if (!mergeBudgetAdmits(budget, [merge.span])) continue;` and `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(...))) continue;`. merge.test.ts covers only the second (RefusingStore / ToggleRefusingStore). A paste that overspends the local budget — the case the comment says is 'where the map's budget is most easily overspent' — has no test, and the running `budget` update after each accepted block is likewise unverified.

samples.summary: clearCopyBuffer on sortFilterByColumn has no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds `this.clearCopyBuffer()` to the sort path with the rationale that a sort renumbers snapshotted cells. merge.test.ts adds copy-buffer tests for insert (`insertRows`), reorder (`moveRows`), undo/redo and remote revalidation, but I found no test asserting `getCopyRange()` is undefined after `sortFilterByColumn`; grep for getCopyRange shows hits only in merge.test.ts and clipboard.test.ts (the pre-existing cut-mode test). A regression would let a paste relocate merges from stale coordinates after a sort.

samples.summary: View-layer changes (reorder refusal gating selection, paste no longer clearing the buffer, revalidateCopyBuffer call) are untested
samples.evidence: Three behavior changes land in view/worksheet.ts and view/spreadsheet.ts: the drag-reorder `.then((moved) => { if (!moved) return; ... })` selection guard, removal of `clearCopyBuffer()` after paste in both views, and the new `this.sheet!.revalidateCopyBuffer()` in the remote-change handler. The model-level equivalents are tested in merge.test.ts, but I found no view test (worksheet-mouse.test.ts, worksheet-keymap.test.ts, keymap.test.ts, spreadsheet-*) asserting any of them. A regression would show a selection at a destination rows never reached, or a stale clipboard surviving a remote structural edit.

samples.summary: assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze is only tested on the row axis
samples.evidence: worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts adds a refusal test and an allowed test, both with `axis: 'row'` and `frozenRows`. The column branch (`frozenCols`, `axis: 'column'`) of the new check is never exercised, even though the insert/delete snap tests do cover a column case. A column-axis mistake in `moveMergeMap`/`crossesFreezePane` usage would ship unnoticed.

samples.summary: snapshotMergesIn's partial-clip filter has no test
samples.evidence: `snapshotMergesIn` filters out blocks the copied range only clips (`isRangeInRange`). The doc comment concedes the UI cannot reach that case, so only a programmatic caller can — and no test in merge.test.ts copies a range that clips a merged block and asserts the block is absent from the pasted layout. If the filter were dropped, a partial block would be re-created at the destination with no failing test.

samples.summary: ReadOnlyStore.setMerge now returns false, changing engine behavior in read-only mode, with no test
samples.evidence: Previously `setMerge` was a silent no-op and `Sheet.mergeSelection` continued to record the merge in memory; now `mergeSelection` returns false early on a falsy store result, so a read-only sheet records nothing. I grepped packages/sheets/test for `ReadOnlyStore` (only store.test.ts data-validations) and for `merge` in worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts (no matches). Nothing pins the new read-only behavior either way.

samples.summary: Assertion on constant arithmetic adds no coverage
samples.evidence: `expect(budget.coveredCells + MaxMergedCells).toBeGreaterThan(MaxMergeCoveredCells)` compares two imported constants plus a literal-derived value; it holds regardless of whether any merge-budget code works. It documents the fixture's intent but cannot fail on a behavior regression — the neighbouring `mergeBudgetAdmits` assertion is what carries the test.

finding.evidence: `setMerge` now returns a boolean, spends `mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(others), [span])` against a `projectedMerges()` map, and `beginBatch`/`endBatch` maintain a new `batchMerges` overlay that `deleteMerge` also reads. verdict.reason: Verified independently: yorkie-store.ts:975-1040 implements projectedMerges()/batchMerges overlay, the `key !== sref` re-anchor exclusion, the mergeBudgetAdmits false-return path, and deleteMerge's projection read; beginBatch/endBatch at :1229-1240 maintain the overlay. Repo-wide greps for projectedMerges/batchMerges/mergeBudgetAdmits find no test file at all. Every test-side setMerge/deleteMerge call belongs to a different store: packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts (Sheet/MemStore), packages/cli/test/sheets-view.test.ts, backend worksheet specs, and the visual harness scenario sheet-scenarios.tsx:229-230 which uses `new MemStore(grid)` — so even the sheet-merge-layout visual baselines never touch YorkieStore. The only YorkieStore suites (yorkie-axis-order, yorkie-cut-paste, yorkie-store-read-only, plus helper-driven comments-concurrency/cross-sheet) contain no merge usage; a case-insensitive `merge` grep over packages/frontend/tests yields only a `$.sheets.tab-1.merges.0` path string in remote-change-utils.test.ts:18 and unrelated docs/twMerge hits, and yorkie-cut-paste.test.ts uses beginBatch/endBatch (lines 28-31, 62-67) without ever writing a merge. No test can fail if the budget projection or overlay is wrong, and the failure mode is a silently dropped merge/paste layout — a data-affecting, user-visible gap, so major in the test-adequacy lane.

mergedFrom.summary: Batched deleteMerge now consults the projected map instead of the document; no test covers delete-after-set-within-one-batch

finding.summary: The delta's real new logic — YorkieStore.setMerge budgeting, refusal, and the batchMerges/projectedMerges overlay — has no test anywhere
finding.evidence: This delta rewrites YorkieStore.setMerge to (a) spend the merge budget at call time against a projected map, (b) exclude the anchor's own existing span when re-anchoring, (c) return false on refusal, and (d) track queued writes in `batchMerges` so a paste's many blocks are budgeted against the map the batch is building. No test exercises any of it: grep for `setMerge|projectedMerges|batchMerges` matches no file under packages/frontend/tests (only src + sheets tests), and a case-insensitive grep for `merge` across packages/frontend/tests returns only docs/slides/utils tests. The sheets tests added here use MemStore subclasses whose setMerge is overridden wholesale, so they never touch the budget arithmetic. If the overlay or the self-exclusion is wrong, a paste can overspend the cap (storing a merge map a later load cannot walk) or silently drop a legal re-anchor — both data-affecting and invisible to the green suite.

verdict.reason: The behavior exists as described in yorkie-store.ts: projectedMerges() overlays batchMerges on the document map (lines 975-991), setMerge excludes the anchor's own existing span (1016-1018), refuses by returning false via mergeBudgetAdmits/mergeBudgetOf (1019-1021), records queued writes in batchMerges (1033), and beginBatch/endBatch allocate/clear it (1232, 1240). No test exercises any of it. Repo-wide grep for setMerge|projectedMerges|batchMerges hits only src files plus sheets/cli/backend tests. I also checked the co-located-test convention this repo uses (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/*.test.* — five files, none on yorkie-store), and every file importing yorkie-store (only helpers/single-user-yorkie.ts, two-user-spreadsheet-yorkie.ts, cross-sheet-yorkie.ts, yorkie-axis-order.test.ts, yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts, docs read-only test, sheet-view.tsx, revision-preview.tsx); following those helper chains, a case-insensitive grep for "merge" over all of packages/frontend/tests yields only remote-change-utils.test.ts (a path-string classification case, line 17-18) and unrelated docs/slides/utils tests. yorkie-cut-paste.test.ts uses beginBatch and YorkieStore but contains no merge content, so the paste/batch overlay path is untested. The sheets tests confirm the gap rather than closing it: merge.test.ts:480-484 and 506-513 override setMerge wholesale on MemStore (testing only the engine's reaction to a refusal), and MemStore.setMerge (memory.ts:586-589) always returns true with no budget logic; merge.test.ts:17-50 tests the budget helpers as pure functions, not the store's overlay or self-exclusion. Blocking as major under this lens: an overspent overlay can persist a merge map beyond MaxMergeEntries that a later load must walk, and a wrong self-exclusion silently drops a legal re-anchor — data-affecting and invisible to a green suite.
